A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EpiMine work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated material and accounting for percentage scaling.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on three thematic news corpora, component ablations, article-selection sensitivity results, and a qualitative episode-detection case study.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds a No LLM ablation and a human–LLM annotation-agreement study.

M1.justification: The four-stage pipeline, discriminative co-occurrence calculation, article ranking, clustering, LLM summarization, harmonic-mean representations, and confidence-based classification remain unchanged. No LLM is an experimental ablation, not a replacement for the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Terrorism/Attacks, Natural Disasters, and Political Events corpora, with matching event lists and Table 1 statistics. The added annotation audit samples existing coverage rather than introducing another dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds No LLM as an evaluated comparison control. EMiner, K-means, EvMine, and their existing LLM-augmented comparisons remain unchanged, as do the standalone Claude and GPT-4 comparators in Table 5.

E3.justification: V2 adds a control that classifies the full dataset with confidence using representations from unsummarized episode clusters. Appendix D also introduces an annotation-validation protocol involving four annotators, 25 articles, and 300 segments, merging multiple/no-episode labels into -1. The principal top-5 evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new No LLM ablation isolates LLM summarization while retaining full-corpus classification, unlike the existing EpiMine-Top analysis. V2 also adds annotation-quality validation. The previous component ablations, article-selection sensitivity analysis, and Hong Kong case study are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly reports statistical annotation-reliability estimates using Cohen's kappa and three intraclass-correlation variants. Both versions already average the principal results over ten LLM-generation runs; v2 adds no confidence intervals or variability estimates for those results.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds No LLM results and changes No Confidence's Politics 5-F1 from 0.3385 to 24.77% (0.2477), reversing its ordering with EpiMine. Table 6 adds kappa = 0.614 and ICC values 0.772, 0.772, and 0.773. Other retained Table 2 values match after scaling, and Table 3 values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The episode definition corrects the impossible range '2 >= k >= 20' in v1 Definition 3.1 to '2 <= k <= 20' in v2 Definition 1. The remaining mathematical definitions and formulas are retained or relocated; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a novel episode-detection task, the same unsupervised EpiMine framework, three thematic datasets, and a 59.2% average gain over baselines. V2 emphasizes LLM synergy and context limitations without substantively changing these central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting LLM context limitations to fragment selection and explaining K-means' relative strength on semantically distinct natural-disaster episodes. It also refines the confidence–recall discussion. The political-event term-overlap limitation and multilingual future direction were already present.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly documents four graduate-student annotators, manual creation of episode descriptions, and inspection of at least twenty articles per event. Appendix A adds a two-RTX-A6000 hardware disclosure for non-API models. Existing model names, hyperparameters, prompts, preprocessing, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion substantially shifts toward LLM-assisted extraction and context handling. V2 removes the dedicated topic-discovery survey and numerous associated references, while adding work on LLM extraction, long-context limitations, and retrieval robustness, including Pai, Gao, Li, Liu, and Shen et al. (2024).

P1.justification: V2 changes the title and extensively rewrites and condenses the abstract, introduction, related work, and methodology. Detailed settings, baseline descriptions, salience scoring, and preprocessing move into appendices. It adds dedicated limitations and acknowledgements sections and moves the ethics statement into the main text.

P2.justification: V2 substantially changes typography and page layout, redraws the framework in Figure 2, adds explanatory annotations to Figure 1, and color-codes episode correspondences in Table 5. Table 2 is rescaled and reformatted with an additional row, and Table 6 is added. The sensitivity plot retains its existing results.

improvement.justification: The full-pipeline No LLM ablation and annotation-agreement audit provide useful additional evidence about component contributions and dataset reliability. Clearer annotation documentation and revised diagrams also help. These are incremental gains: the core method and principal findings remain stable, and the revised No Confidence Politics F1 is unexplained.
